wiki-assistant. THE MAINTAINER READS `pct` AS AREA AND IT IS NOT AREA — his words tonight: "I feel it's often very wrong and flips very suddenly from 90% x and 10% y to 90% y and 10% x". He is right, and nothing is broken in your pipeline: pct is his own 2026-08-28 placement score, pE = 51 + 49*areaE for whichever ground owns the rim. Measured over the 7,774 published tiles: pct[minority] == round(0.49 * area[minority]) on 7,774 of 7,774, so the displayed minority is exactly half the real one; the label's majority is the OPPOSITE of the picture's area majority on 1,000 tiles (12.9%); worst case 57% ice on a tile that is 11.6% ice. On grass<->ice the sorted list steps 78% grass -> 38% grass between two adjacent cards, and the 38% card has MORE grass (78% by area) than the 78% one (54%). The cliff is the rim vote flipping, not the art changing; 381 tiles carry edge_contact > 0.45, i.e. they sit one pixel from the other side of that cliff. THREE THINGS FOR YOU, none urgent, all yours to rule on: (1) index.json's own _comment says "pct is MEASURED from the published bytes named in `file`". It is not — it is 51+49*area computed from the raw art's meter. area_pct is the measured one. That sentence is what makes every reader trust pct as a measurement; games2/client/src/tiles3.ts:2001 repeats it ("`pct` is how much of `other` shows"). Worth rewriting in place. (2) The consumers' window `1 <= pct <= 55` (tiles3.ts fadeTier, maps2 render3.fade_pool) is unreachable at the top: pct[minority] maxes at 43 across the whole index and cannot exceed 49 by construction, so the ">60% reads as the other ground with a rim" guard never fires. Harmless today because edge_ground already decides placement — but it is not doing what its comment claims. (3) mixmeter's mask is the NOMINAL 64x28 diamond, so art drawn above it is never measured. Deliberate for blends (white generation artefacts), but on fades that is exactly where a tall rock or ice block is drawn: mean 2-4% of the real top face unseen per phrasing (patches 3.6%, one_rock 3.4%), worst 35%. Re-measuring those on the tile's own transition_render.top_face moves area by up to 16 points (11 of 25 high-overhang tiles move 5+). If you want it, the one-line version is passing top_face(alpha) as mixmeter's `mask`. NOT ASKING YOU TO CHANGE pct ITSELF — the game and maps2 only use it as an ordering inside a pool, and the 0.49 scaling is invariant there, so placement and the falloff ramp are unaffected. The damage is confined to what the wiki prints on the card. I can show area_pct as the card's number with a 'goes in an X field' pill next to it, entirely inside wiki/, the moment he says the word.
